power.thresholds_short: Short dips are ignored; runs under 10 s don't count.

rule_sentence.pause: {type}: the power stays below {below} for {seconds} – ignore the first {ignore}.
rule_sentence.cycling: {type}: at {level} or more for less than {share} of {window} – ignore the first {ignore}.
rule_sentence.drop: {type} at least {percent} within {window} – ignore the first {ignore}.
rule_sentence.knee: {type}: over the last {window} at least {factor} as fast as in the {baseline} before – ignore the first {ignore}.
rule.all_hint: It switches off: kettle, toaster. It pauses: appliances that pause when done. It stops cycling: thermostat appliances. The power falls by / the trend bends steeper downwards: e.g. a moka pot. The trend flattens out, turns upwards or bends steeper upwards: the curve changes its direction. Is below its trend: e.g. a moka pot, adapts to the sensor's scatter. Is above its trend: something switches on at the end. Plateau: a rice cooker switching to keep warm. It has run for / has used: only for very regular runs. Switch-on spikes are ignored for the first seconds. More steps: "it is done" after several rules met one after another.
runs.title: Runs
runs.none_hint: Each run is stored with its power curve when the appliance switches off. Earlier runs are read once from the sensor's history, as far as the recorder kept it.
runs.running: Running for {time} – the curve updates every few seconds.
runs.picked_up: The curve starts at {time}: Home Assistant restarted, or the station was saved, during the run.
runs.sensor.hint: A rule notices a change only when the sensor reports it.
runs.sensor.more: Much of the time between "done" and the ring is the sensor's: one that reports every 10 s notices a change up to 10 s late. Scatter makes small changes hard to tell from noise, so the rules then need larger thresholds.
power.done_hint: Done can come before off: a moka pot's coffee is ready while the plate is still hot.
onoff.title: On and off
onoff.sentence: It runs while the power is above {on_above} and counts as off after {off_after} below.
runs.after_save: Runs appear here once the station is saved
runs.after_save_hint: Then its earlier runs are read once from the sensor's history, and every new run is stored with its curve.
runs.sensor_changed: These runs were recorded with {old}. You picked {new}: after saving they stay, marked “other sensor”; new runs come from the new one.
outcome.never: never done – rings only when it switches off ({time})
preview.title: Your draft on the {count} stored runs:
preview.title_one: Your draft on the stored run:
preview.never: {count} never done – they would ring only when switched off
preview.never_one: 1 never done – it would ring only when switched off
preview.marks_later: Whether that is too early or too late can only be told once runs are marked as done.
outcome.open: does not switch off within the recorded curve with these settings
rule.trend_hint: Done when the power falls clearly below the line of its slow fall before – e.g. a moka pot; how clearly follows the sensor's scatter.
rule_verb.trend: the power is below its trend
rule_sentence.trend: {type} by at least {factor} its scatter, the trend taken over {baseline} – ignore the first {ignore}.
learn.ask: Was it done somewhere in this run?
learn.ask_hint: Click the curve where it was done, or use the button and move the mark.
learn.drag_hint: your mark – drag it, or ← → 1 s, Shift 10 s
learn.now_hint: The mark can be moved once the run is stored.
learn.left_out: Left out of learning: it stays stored, but does not count for suggestions or “on time”.
preview.marked_title: Your draft on the {count} marked runs:
preview.saved_title: The saved settings on the {count} marked runs:
preview.unmarked: {count} without a mark are only compared.
learn.suggest_need: Mark when it was done in at least {min} runs ({count} of {min}).
learn.tolerance: {count} runs marked · on time is up to {field} after the mark
learn.searching: Trying all rules on your runs …
learn.used: From “Suggest from my runs”. Save to use it, or Discard.
learn.none: No rule fits these marks within the tolerance. Check the marks, or allow more time.
learn.outlier_hint: Its mark at {time} is where the best suggestion does not ring within {tol} s – the mark may be off.
rule.rise_hint: Done when the power rises clearly above the line of its course before – something that switches on at the end, e.g. a pump or a fan.
rule_verb.rise: the power is above its trend
rule_sentence.rise: {type} by at least {factor} its scatter, the trend taken over {baseline} – ignore the first {ignore}.
rule.plateau_hint: Done when the power stays at one level for a while after it changed – e.g. a rice cooker switching to keep warm.
rule_sentence.plateau: {type}: within ± {factor} its scatter for {seconds} – ignore the first {ignore}.
preview.unmarked_one: 1 without a mark is only compared.
learn.stale: Your marks or settings changed since – suggest again for current suggestions.
learn.not_usable: Too few marked runs can be used with these on and off settings (each needs to switch on and off within its curve).
rule.flatten_hint: Done when the power falls a factor slower than before, or no longer – a curve that levels off.
rule_sentence.flatten: {type}: over the last {window} at least {factor} slower than in the {baseline} before – ignore the first {ignore}.
rule.upturn_hint: Done when the power starts to rise after it fell or stayed – something switches on again.
rule_sentence.upturn: {type}: the power rises over the last {window}, at least {factor} more than still counts as flat, after it did not rise in the {baseline} before – ignore the first {ignore}.
rule.steeper_up_hint: Done when the power rises a factor faster than before – e.g. heating that switches to a higher stage.
rule_sentence.steeper_up: {type}: over the last {window} at least {factor} as fast as in the {baseline} before – ignore the first {ignore}.
power.done_steps: It is done after these steps
steps.add_hint: it is looked for once the step before was met
steps.hint: Each step is looked for once the step before was met and looks at nothing before it – its "ignore" counts from there. It is done when the last step is met. Time and energy count from the start of the run.
learn.failed: The search failed – see the Home Assistant log.
learn.lost: The search was interrupted (Home Assistant restarted) – start it again.
